summary: Cross-vendor adversarial panel over the intent-to-completion spec-gate artifacts (spec.md rev 12 + goals.md), bytes embedded verbatim

result.summary: One blocker survives in-tree verification and it is structural: §7.4's `required-successor` doctor check FAILs while the named successor is not `completion: complete`, and this repo's CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `test` job step "Doctor": `node bin/doctor.mjs`, exit 1 on any ERROR per `bin/doctor.mjs:76`) runs that doctor on every push and every `v*` tag — so from the moment this run's archive (carrying `required_successor{v10-validation}`) is pushed in §10.2, main CI is red until `v10-validation` completes, and `v10-validation`'s own tag CI is red, which fails its mandatory `install` step (`gh run watch --exit-status`) → `deploy_failed` → skip/abort only → it can never reach `complete`. Outcome 7 is unreachable as written. Beyond that, eleven should-fix items hold up: the corrective-release path publishes an unreviewed fix (the S5 mitigation only covers the first pass); the bootstrap walk is prose while its rehearsal is a script, so the rehearsal proves a different executor; `done: none` is named in four places and reconciled with §7.1's mandatory-groups rule in none; `context_watch.focus` is an inert knob inside the spec that exists to close that class; the `high` critic cadence can be satisfied with one or two critic passes because rounds are neither sealed nor size-bounded; stage-produced commits are path-unrestricted while the final assessment binds to the pre-commit sha; the v10 finish never pushes the archive (verified: `lib/finish-step.mjs` ends at `commitBundle` + `op: stop`); the `bootstrap_step` schema has no shape for a corrective second pass; a single failed critic dispatch licenses `exhausted` with no retry; the env-scan guard misses destructured/bracket access; and the install flip's cross-repo blast radius (single `current` symlink in `bin/install-pi.mjs`, real `auto_compact` block in `/srv/dev/xcvr-tools-fresh/.masterplan.yaml`) is not acknowledged. Four reviewer claims were dropped after checking the tree — most importantly the CI job-skip hazard (`release-publish` has `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`, unskippable on a tag run) and the WORKLOG PR-merge conflict (the run branch is created from local `main`, which already contains the four non-bundle commits). The rest of §7/§10's git mechanics held under tracing, consistent with the failure-case reviewer's assessment.

findings.claim: The `required-successor` doctor check is self-referential through this repo's CI: it FAILs while `v10-validation` is not `completion: complete`, CI runs the doctor on every push and tag, and the successor's mandatory install step waits on its own tag CI — so the required successor can never archive complete and main CI goes red permanently.
findings.failure: §10.2 pushes this run's archive carrying `required_successor{slug: v10-validation}` → GitHub main's next CI run executes `node bin/doctor.mjs` (ci.yml `test` job) → ERROR → exit 1 (bin/doctor.mjs:76) → red. `v10-validation` seeds, works, tags v10.0.x; its tag CI runs the same doctor while its own bundle is non-archived → red → `gh run watch --exit-status` (§7.1 install group) non-zero → `deploy_failed` → retry is a no-op, `skip` archives incomplete, `abort` archives nothing. `completion: complete` is unreachable; Outcome 7's second sentence can never be satisfied; every later push to main stays red.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md §7.4 (lines 497–500) × §10 step 3 × .github/workflows/ci.yml `test` job "Doctor" step (needed by `release-publish`) × §7.1 install group `gh run watch --exit-status`
findings.fix_direction: FAIL only when the named bundle is absent or archived-but-not-complete; a successor bundle that exists and is non-archived (in progress) is OK/INFO. Alternatively make the check WARN. Either way add the in-progress-successor case to the `resume-brief` doctor suite in §11, and pair it with the post-archive push fix below so GitHub's copy can ever see `complete`.

findings.claim: The corrective-release path (§10.3) re-runs steps 4/6/7 but never step 2, so a fix triggered by a finish-time failure is tagged and installed on both surfaces with no pre-publish verify, adversarial review, or goal assessment — the exact ordering S5 was folded to prevent — and on the first pass the reviewed sha (T) is not the tagged sha (T + release.mjs commit).
findings.failure: Finish-time goal check returns `partial`; fix commits land on the branch; `scripts/release.mjs --version=10.0.1` tags the new tip; steps 4/6/7 publish and install 10.0.1 on Pi and the Claude cache; only afterwards does the re-entered finish run verify/review over `main..tip`. If the fix is wrong, both daily-driver surfaces run it before any review, and the Claude surface has no downgrade lever (A25).
findings.location: spec.md §10.1 steps 2–3 (review at tip, then release commit) and §10.3 corrective-release row ("steps 4, 6 and 7 re-run")
findings.fix_direction: Corrective pass must re-run step 2 (pre-publish verify + cross-vendor review + G1–G5 assessment) at the new tip before step 3, recorded as `bootstrap_step` events. For sha identity, either run `release.mjs` before the review so receipts bind to the tagged commit, or assert in the walk that `tag^{commit}` differs from the reviewed sha by a CHANGELOG-only commit (release.mjs never bumps, so that is the only legal delta). Not a blocker: tag CI re-runs tests+doctor on the tagged commit before `install-pi`, and the finish still reviews post-publish.

findings.claim: The bootstrap wave — the only irreversible, fleet-shared-state procedure in the design — has no deterministic driver: its preconditions (fetch/ancestor, per-commit audit, dirty tree, digest checks) are enforced only by prose read live by the model, the `bootstrap_step` schema validates a record after the action fired, and the rehearsal script exercises a different executor than the live walk.
findings.failure: `scripts/rehearse-v9-finish.sh` passes on fixtures. The live walk is then executed step-by-step from ~150 lines of §10 prose; step 4 blocks minutes on CI (a compaction-risk turn §9 exists to protect, yet §10 is not in §12's `commands/masterplan.md` touch list). After a mid-walk compaction the agent re-derives position from the event list; a step-5 push made without the fetch/ancestor precondition, or a rebase against the wrong tip, lands on `origin main` — shared by three hosts per /srv/dev/AGENTS.md — before any code refuses it. `mp event` (bin/masterplan.mjs:1037) is a generic append; §12 lists no bootstrap verb.
findings.location: spec.md:627–632 (§10.1 step 1), :914–919 (§12 touch surface), §10.1.1 rehearsal; contrast lib/dispatch-wave.mjs, lib/wave-commit.mjs, docs/internals/wave-dispatch.md
findings.fix_direction: Run the live walk through the same step functions as the rehearsal script (a `--live` mode with real targets), so the rehearsal proves the executor that will run; add an `mp bootstrap next`/`status` verb that computes the next unexecuted step from the event log and refuses out-of-order or precondition-failing steps before the git/gh action fires. Stop calling it a "wave" — plan-annotations wave semantics (disjoint `files`, `dispatch-wave`, two-phase commit) do not apply; name it a bootstrap stage so plan.md and resume tooling do not import the wrong model. If the operator's A8 prompt-first choice is kept for this step, record the residual risk as an explicit assumption row.

findings.claim: `done: none` is named as the explicit opt-out in four places but is never reconciled with §7.1's rule that `release`/`install`/`live_check` are mandatory groups or with §7.2's `no_definition_of_done` trigger, leaving seed acceptance, deploy-stage behavior, and completion class undefined.
findings.failure: A repo with no deploy surface sets `done: none` (e.g. /srv/dev/xcvr-tools-fresh, which today has no `done:` key). Depending on the implementation's reading: the seed rejects it (§4.1 schema is an object), or `no_definition_of_done` opens on every finish ("no `done:` block"), or every run in that repo archives `incomplete` forever (§7.1 mandatory groups), or — worst — it archives `complete` with zero deploy evidence, contradicting Outcome 3. §11's "`done: none` accepted" test cannot be written against any of these.
findings.location: spec.md:416 (§7.1 mandatory-groups rule) vs :499 (§7.4), :806 (§11 config suite), :869 (§11 doctor suite), :1065 (N14 disposition)
findings.fix_direction: Define the sentinel: seed accepts `done: none` as distinct from the object schema; the deploy stage skips the mandatory-group enforcement and `no_definition_of_done` does not open; the run archives under a distinct class (e.g. `complete:no-deploy-surface` or `incomplete:no_deploy_surface`, chosen deliberately against Outcome 3) that `runs list`/`mp status`/doctor print; add the case to `deploy-commit-identity`/`finish-replay`.

findings.claim: `context_watch.focus` is itself an inert knob: §4.1 declares it operator-settable with a default, but §9's rendering always emits the fixed masterplan-authored template and no consumer of the configured value is described.
findings.failure: Operator sets `context_watch: {focus: "keep the auth-token flow"}`; every gate line still prints `recommend: /compact run <slug>, phase <phase>, gate <id>; keep goals.md outcome + open gate; drop tool output`. `test/knob-contract.test.mjs` applied to this nested key (§4.4 lists `context_watch.threshold` as an example observable but not `focus`) either fails on the spec's own field or the field is quietly exempted — Problem §1's defect class reproduced inside the spec written to close it (G4).
findings.fix_direction: Either render the configured `focus` (operator value overrides or is appended to the auto-generated template) with its own knob-contract test and `<!-- knob -->` marker, or drop `focus` from the schema and make `context_watch` `{threshold}` only.

findings.claim: The `high`-complexity guarantee "critic after every intent round" is denominated in ledger rounds, but rounds are neither sealed nor size-bounded: `mp interview ask` accepts the current round number after its questions are answered, and the floor counts questions while a round may hold four — so an 8–20 question interview can be `converged` with one or two critic passes and no round-to-round adaptivity.
findings.failure: (a) Ask Q1 `--round=1`, answer, ask Q2 `--round=1` (permitted: only an *earlier* round's unanswered question blocks), … Q8 all round 1, one draft, one clean critic → `converged` at `high` with one critic over eight separate AUQ exchanges. (b) Following the fleet's mandatory batching policy (/srv/workflows/policy/auq.md:10, ~/AGENTS.md:64), round 1 = 4 intent questions, round 2 = 2 intent + 2 design → floor 8, intent floor 6, one design pick, two receipts → `converged` after two human exchanges whose questions could not adapt to each other's answers — the shallow probing the topic line complains about, with a ledger that reads as rigorous.
findings.location: spec.md §5.3 (`ask` refusal set: "a round number other than the current or the next round"), §4.2 lines 118–131 (round definition, floor in answered questions), §5.4 `converged` row
findings.fix_direction: Seal a round on its first answer/draft/critic (the next ask must use r+1) so one AUQ call maps 1:1 to a ledger round; denominate the floor (or at least the `high` cadence) in intent rounds, or cap questions per intent round below the AUQ maximum; optionally have the critic's clean verdict also judge whether round count/batch size shows iterative depth.

findings.claim: Stage-produced commits (§7.3 (b)) are unrestricted in what they may touch, while the final assessment and `completion_confirmed` stay bound to `deploy_base_sha`, so the assessed sha can differ from the installed code without the audit noticing.
findings.failure: A repo's `release` step runs `npm run generate && git add -A && git commit` and the generator changes application code. The receipt records `commits: [sha]`, `base_after` advances, no `base moved` error fires; `run_final_check` and `completion_confirmed` still bind to the pre-generation `deploy_base_sha`; the run archives `complete` having assessed code that is not what was tagged and installed. A30 generalizes a rule that is only safe for the sample (version files + CHANGELOG).
findings.fix_direction: Restrict stage-produced commits to a declared non-behavioral allowlist (`version_from` file + CHANGELOG; anything else is `base moved`), or advance the bound sha to `base_after` and re-run the final assessment at that sha before `completion_confirmed`.

findings.claim: The v10 finish flow has no post-archive push, so a successor's `completion: complete` exists only on the machine that produced it — unlike the bootstrap walk (§10.2), which pushes explicitly — and GitHub's doctor keeps seeing the successor as absent/incomplete.
findings.failure: `v10-validation`'s `done:` install group pushes main before archive; the archive commit lands on local main and finish-step returns `op: stop` (lib/finish-step.mjs:397–408: `commitBundle` then `stop`, push is shell-side only for the `pr` choice). `origin/main` never receives the completion; the other two host-local clones and every CI run on GitHub main evaluate `required-successor` against a bundle that is absent or not complete. Even with the blocker's exemption in place, CI on main goes red at the successor's archive-time push gap.
findings.location: spec.md §7.2 op table (ends at `archive`) vs §10 step 2 (explicit post-archive push); lib/finish-step.mjs:397–408
findings.fix_direction: Add a post-archive push step to §7.2 (or an `archive` group in `done:` that runs after archive under the same authorize/started/done ledger), and a `finish-replay` case asserting origin receives the archive commit.

findings.claim: The `bootstrap_step` schema (monotone step order; a repeated step refused unless `status: recovered`) has no shape for the corrective pass, whose second `release`/`push`/`install`/`claude_surface`/`pr_merge` sequence follows a successful first pass and is triggered by a finish-time event, not a `bootstrap_step` failure.
findings.failure: First `release` succeeds. Finish-time goal check returns `partial`. The corrective `release` event is a same-named repeat with no preceding `failed` bootstrap_step to recover from and out of monotone order after `pr_merge`; it is either refused or forced under a false `recovered` label. G6 reads "the latest `bootstrap_step {step: release}`" for its version; if the event cannot be legally recorded, G6 assesses v10.0.0 and stays `partial`.
findings.location: spec.md §10.1 step 1 (schema rules) vs §10.3 corrective-release row and §11 `v9-to-v10-bootstrap` ("a repeated or out-of-order step is refused, `status: recovered` is accepted")
findings.fix_direction: Define a corrective-pass shape (e.g. `pass: 2` or `status: corrective` opening a fresh monotone sequence from `release`, with the triggering event id recorded) and add it to the `v9-to-v10-bootstrap` fixtures.

findings.claim: A single failed critic dispatch at `medium`/`high` immediately makes `exhausted` a valid exit with no retry and no operator question — the only degradation path in the spec that does not fail closed or route through an AUQ.
findings.failure: Frontier-lane rate limit on one critic dispatch → `critic_unavailable` → `mp interview end --reason=exhausted` accepted with the floor met; remaining unknowns become assumptions and goals freeze without the operator ever being asked, at the complexity level whose whole purpose is to probe until understood. Fleet policy (~/AGENTS.md "Fail closed") treats an unavailable reviewer as an error to surface, not a state to proceed from.
findings.location: spec.md §5.4 terminal-states table (`exhausted`: "or critic mode is `unavailable`"), §4.2 critic column ("until clean, cap, or unavailable")
findings.fix_direction: Require at least one retry (and, under `gated`, an AUQ naming the error) before `critic_unavailable` may license `exhausted`; record the retry attempts in the event.

findings.claim: The knob-inventory scan's stated escape hatch is narrower than the language allows, and the contract test has no held-constant rule, so the guard's "any future inert knob fails the suite" claim is not established.
findings.failure: `const { MP_NEW_MODE } = process.env` or `process.env[key]` has no literal `process.env.NAME` member for the lexical inventory and is not the `const env = process.env` alias §4.4 rejects — an inert env knob never enters the inventory. Separately, a contract test whose two runs differ in the target knob and, via shared fixture setup, in complexity passes on the other input's difference.
findings.location: spec.md §4.4 ("rejects aliased `process.env` access … (`const env = process.env`)"; contract test definition)
findings.fix_direction: Reject any non-literal `process.env` access in `lib/`/`bin/` (destructuring, bracket, alias, `Object.entries(process.env)`) or route all env reads through one `readEnv(name)` helper the scan enumerates; give contract tests a harness that varies exactly one input and fails if the fixtures differ elsewhere.

findings.claim: The Pi install root and the Claude plugin cache are host/account-wide singletons, so steps 4 and 6 flip every masterplan-using repo's `mp` binary mid-session, but §10 and its rehearsal reason only about this repo and the `publish_ack` AUQ does not name the cross-repo window.
findings.failure: bin/install-pi.mjs:12 swaps one `<install-root>/current` symlink for all repos. After step 4, a session mid-run in /srv/dev/xcvr-tools-fresh (real `.masterplan.yaml` with `auto_compact: {enabled, interval, focus}`, no `done:`) runs a v9 sequencer against the v10 binary: `mp seed` now refuses without `--overlap-review`, unknown seed flags die at bin/masterplan.mjs:588, `auto_compact` is aliased to `context_watch` with `enabled`/`interval` discarded as unknown nested keys, and its next finish opens `no_definition_of_done`. Nothing scans for in-progress bundles elsewhere before the flip. (Impact is narrower than reviewer 5 stated: the removed flags are seed-only, so an in-flight session does not reissue them.)
findings.location: spec.md §10 steps 4 and 6, §10.1.1 rehearsal scope, A13/A29; bin/install-pi.mjs:12, bin/masterplan.mjs:588, /srv/dev/xcvr-tools-fresh/.masterplan.yaml
findings.fix_direction: Add a cross-repo note to §10: the `publish_ack` AUQ text names that every masterplan repo on the host switches binaries; before step 4 scan the fleet's known repos for non-archived bundles (or accept the window in an assumption row); document the `auto_compact` alias loss (`enabled`/`interval` dropped) in the warning text.

findings.claim: The Claude-surface live check proves the plugin cache (version binary + registry-drift doctor), not that the currently loaded session is running v10; the spec should state that limit rather than imply a loaded-surface proof.
findings.failure: Operator runs `/plugin update masterplan` but `/reload-plugins` fails silently; both checks pass against the cache directory; the current session keeps v9 behavior until it ends. Practical exposure is small — Outcome 7 and §7.1 define the Claude surface as the plugin cache, the current session is the one finishing the run, and the successor requires a fresh session — which is why this is not the blocker reviewer 1 rated it.
findings.location: spec.md §7.1 `user_only`/`live_check` Claude steps, §10 step 6, goals.md G6
findings.fix_direction: State in §7.1/Outcome 7 that the Claude-surface proof is cache-level and that a fresh session is the loaded-surface proof, or add a required fresh-session round-trip (e.g. `/masterplan version` in a new session) before the check is recorded.

findings.claim: A sibling push to `origin/main` between the step-5 push and the gate leaves only a bare "stop" (§10.2 equality rule) with no named resumption path that preserves `main..tip` for the review of record.
findings.failure: Another host pushes an unrelated commit after step 5; at the gate `origin/main` ≠ the latest recorded PR-merge sha → stop. The §10.3 table has a row for a rejected step-5 push ("reconcile by hand") and for a foreign commit on local main, but none for this state, so the operator has no instruction for reaching the rebase without widening the audit.
findings.location: spec.md §10.2 ("a different remote tip means someone else moved GitHub `main`: stop") vs §10.3 table
findings.fix_direction: Add a §10.3 row: fetch, verify the foreign commit is outside the bundle and the branch, re-record the equality target as the new remote tip after operator ack, and proceed to the rebase; rehearse it.

findings.claim: The `assumed` rows an `exhausted` exit owes the spec are enforced only by reviewer attention (already disclosed as N11), though a mechanical diff against the `interview_end` event's id lists is cheap.
findings.failure: Critic returns U1/C1, the next dispatch is unavailable, the interview ends `exhausted` listing both; the author omits C1 from the Assumptions table; the spec gate reviewer misses it; goals-load, plan, and finish proceed with no check comparing the table to the event.
findings.location: spec.md §5.4 last paragraph ("reviewer-enforced at the spec gate; `goals-load` does not parse the spec")
findings.fix_direction: Have `goals-load` (which already receives the spec path at the gate) grep the Assumptions table for each id in the `interview_end` lists and refuse when one is missing.

findings.claim: `mp context-status` reports `unsupported` both when the harness has no transcripts (Pi) and when the transcript is simply not at the expected `<encoded MAIN path>` (a session launched in a subdirectory of MAIN), so the context watch can be silently disabled on the primary harness while looking like the intentional Pi degradation.
findings.failure: Claude Code files transcripts under the cwd at launch; a session started in `<MAIN>/lib` resolves nothing under the MAIN encoding and prints `context: unknown (unsupported)` at every gate; no §11 fixture distinguishes the cases. (Note: lib/paths.mjs has no project-path encoding today — `claudeConfigDir` only — so the "encoding `lib/paths.mjs` already uses" claim will need to be implemented, not reused.)
findings.fix_direction: Add a distinct state or diagnostic (`not-found <expected path>`) and a wrong-cwd fixture; fall back to searching sibling project encodings for the session id.

dropped: Reviewer 1 should-fix: install-group CI check passes on a skipped `release-publish` job. In-tree, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gives `release-publish` `needs: test` and `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`, which is true for every `v*` tag run, so on the tag run the job cannot be skipped and a run-level `success` implies both jobs succeeded (a failed `test` yields run-level failure). §10.1 step 4 additionally records both jobs' conclusions. This claim was already dropped after in-tree verification in the rev-12 panel.

Reviewer 1 should-fix: seed-lock TOCTOU on an "already-fetched" inventory digest. §8 states both recorders recompute the inventory digest at write time and refuse a mismatch (`overlap_review_stale`), and `mp seed` validates under the lock before creating anything, so a concurrent plan.index.json write between the review and the seed is detected, not accepted. The residual recompute→mkdir window (non-seed writers do not take the lock) is exactly what the spec's own "staleness detection, not a lock" wording discloses; no design change is warranted.

Reviewer 2 should-fix (first half): WORKLOG.md PR-merge conflict between local main's non-bundle commits and the branch. The run branch is created by `git worktree add <path> -b masterplan/<slug>` from MAIN's HEAD (lib/worktree.mjs:35–37, no start-point), i.e. from local `main`, which already contains the four non-bundle commits (0b6159d and af52fe8 touch WORKLOG.md; abc3b0a and 5aa3c27 touch policy/workflow-map.json); they are ancestors of the branch tip and cannot conflict at the PR merge, and any later non-bundle commit on main is a §10.3 "foreign commit" stop. The spec's step-5 sentence over-warns but is harmless. The sibling-push-at-gate half survives as a nit.

Reviewer 5's sub-claim that a stale-context session elsewhere "hits `rejectUnknownFlags` hard die() on the removed flags": `--complexity-source` and `--predecessor-transcript` are seed-only flags; an in-flight session never reissues them. The cross-repo blast-radius finding is kept on its remaining, verified legs (singleton `current` symlink, `auto_compact` alias loss, v9 prompt against v10 `mp seed`/finish).
disagreements: `done: none` — reviewer 5 rated blocker, reviewer 1 nit. Evidence favors should-fix: the hole is real and confirmed at all four mentions with no reconciliation against §7.1's mandatory-groups rule or §7.2's trigger, and §11's "`done: none` accepted" test cannot be written without semantics; but this repo will carry a `done:` block, so nothing in Outcome 7 or this run's completion depends on it, and a repo with no deploy surface being unable to reach Outcome 3's `complete` may be the intended reading — the defect is that the spec does not say which.

Bootstrap driver — reviewer 3 (approach-adversary) rated blocker; reviewer 4 (failure-case) traced the same git mechanics and "did not find a load-bearing flaw." Both are right about what they checked: the sequence as written is sound (reviewer 4), and nothing enforces it before an irreversible action fires while the rehearsal exercises a script the live walk does not use (reviewer 3). Should-fix, not blocker: the schema-validated events, the `publish_ack` AUQ, and the rehearsal are real mitigations, and A8 is the operator's recorded choice; the cheapest fix (run the live walk through the rehearsal's step functions) is what makes the rehearsal's proof transfer.

G6 Claude-surface check — reviewer 1 rated blocker ("installed-but-not-running"). Downgraded to nit: Outcome 7 and §7.1 define the Claude surface as the plugin cache and the check does execute the cache binary (rev-11 P9); the only session that can stay stale is the one finishing this run, and the successor requires a fresh session, which loads from the cache. The reviewer's demand for an in-session probe exceeds what the harness exposes deterministically; stating the limit is the proportionate fix.

CI job-skip — reviewer 1 re-raised it as should-fix; the rev-12 panel had dropped it after in-tree verification. The tree (ci.yml `if:` on a `v*` tag) supports the drop; reviewer 1 never saw the workflow file.

Interview rounds — reviewers 1 (round reuse) and 4 (batch size) describe two entrances to the same defect (the `high` critic cadence is denominated in unsealed, unbounded ledger rounds); merged into one should-fix with both failure modes because one accounting change closes both.

Corrective-release review gap — reviewer 1 rated blocker. Should-fix: `release.mjs` never bumps, so the first-pass tagged commit differs from the reviewed one by a CHANGELOG header only, and tag CI re-runs tests+doctor on the tagged commit before `install-pi`; the real gap is the corrective pass, which publishes a code fix with no pre-publish review — a violation of S5's stated rationale that must be fixed for internal consistency, but the finish still reviews it post-publish and the window is the one D2 accepted.
reviewers: failure-case (in-tree verification, no code exists yet — these are design/spec-adequacy findings): revise
